title: Psalm 149: A New Song and a Two-Edged Sword
summary: The assembly of the godly is called to sing a new song, to rejoice in God as their Maker and King, and to praise him with dancing, tambourine, and harp, because he delights in his people and crowns the humble with salvation. The second half pictures the faithful with God's praise in their mouths and a sword in their hands, carrying out the judgment written against the nations and their kings.

line: A new song for the God who delights in his people and crowns the humble, then a picture of the faithful with praise in their mouths and a sword in their hands.
guide: Sing praise that is fresh, not routine: what has God done lately that you have not thanked him for? For a Christian, the plain notes say, the sword is God's word, to be spoken with truth and love.

care.text: Do verses 6 to 9 give God's people a right to take up arms against other nations in his name? No. These lines are the battle poetry of ancient Israel, and they give no one today a warrant for violence of any kind. Such verses have at times been misused to defend religious violence, and that misuse was wrong. Christians read the church's ‘sword’ as the word of God (Ephesians 6:17; Hebrews 4:12), and leave judgment to Christ at his return. That is a reading, and it is how the New Testament itself turns the picture.

stanzas.title: A new song for the King who delights in his people
High praises and a sword: the saints and God's judgment

verses.t: Hallelujah! Sing to the LORD a new song— His praise in the assembly of the godly.
Let Israel rejoice in their Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King.
Let them praise His name with dancing, and make music to Him with tambourine and harp.
For the LORD takes pleasure in His people; He adorns the afflicted with salvation.
Let the saints exult in glory; let them shout for joy upon their beds.
May the high praises of God be in their mouths, and a double-edged sword in their hands,
to inflict vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples,
to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with shackles of iron,
to execute the judgment written against them. This honor is for all His saints. Hallelujah!
